title: Release (Gate 3): release dossier re-measured at the landed SHA and a proof-carrying GitHub PR
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04).

PRODUCT GAP (README + VISION Gate 3 'Approve Release' + Stage 1 'proof-carrying GitHub PR', re-measured 2026-09-04): 'no release gate'. `repository.publish` (acf88616, PR #21) pushes `HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` to a remote the human names and writes `moe-publish-receipt/1` with a GitHub tree link (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts; control room v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx + publish-port.ts) - no pull request is opened (`grep -c "pull" apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher.ts` = 0) and no evidence travels with the push. Coverage (`POST /documents/coverage/read`, http/document-coverage-read.ts) is keyed on the PRD contentSha256, not the shipping git sha. `/runs/read` carries review rounds, verifier receipts, landing and publish per node/goal.

FEATURE: `release.decide` (human-only, Gate 3: 'Is the evidence strong enough to expose this to users?'). Before the decision the daemon builds the RELEASE DOSSIER for the goal at the workspace HEAD sha: per approved criterion -> verifying node -> verifier receipt (command, exit, sha) -> landing commit sha, RE-MEASURED at that sha (each cited commit must be an ancestor of HEAD; anything unmeasurable renders UNKNOWN and is listed, never dropped); review rounds and refusals; the preview decision when one exists (else 'no preview decision' stated); the installed policy revision. Rendered as deterministic markdown; the dossier bytes are stored durable so the PR body can be re-derived and diffed. APPROVE -> push (reuse the publisher) -> open a GitHub pull request whose body IS the dossier (`gh pr create` on the operator's machine, or the REST API with a token the human names on the goal - architect decides; both refuse cleanly) -> `moe-release-receipt/1` {goalId, sha, dossierSha256, prUrl, RELEASED|REFUSED(code)}.

UI: Release card on the opened goal - evidence summary (criteria covered n/m, receipts, landings, preview decision), 'Approve release' arm/confirm like the PUBLISH card, PR link after; Runs shows the release receipt; Needs-you lists goals ready for release. Refusals verbatim: RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING, RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE (naming the missing criteria), RELEASE_PR_FAILED (with the tool's last stderr line).
definitionOfDone: `release.decide` published human-only, MCP-excluded, in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING, RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, RELEASE_PR_FAILED asserted with code + layer.

The dossier generator is a pure function over the ledger reads: a golden test pins the markdown sections (criteria table with node / receipt / landing sha, review rounds, preview decision or its explicit absence); re-measurement proven - a landing sha that is not an ancestor of HEAD renders UNKNOWN, and dossier(shaA) differs from dossier(shaB) on the sha column.

PR creation tested offline through a port with the request (title, base, head, body = dossier bytes) asserted byte-for-byte; the live drive opens a real PR on the UnAI remote or a throwaway GitHub repo - PR URL + receipt in a row comment.
Release card renders the summary + arm/confirm + PR link; Playwright journey against a REAL daemon; `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted.
README 'no release gate' clause and VISION Stage 1 'proof-carrying PR' status updated; runbook documents the `gh` / token prerequisite and its refusal.
Gates quoted with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE COMPOSED FEATURE, read on the DELIVERED code at HEAD 8b785725, not on the design. Two findings recorded as row comments (step 4's own instruction, global rail 21 — no new evidence rows): comment-78438434 and comment-08e78fb3. No production code written.

(a) CAN THE DOSSIER AND THE PR BODY DIVERGE? NO, AND THE TEST THAT PROVES IT IS DISCRIMINATING.
Production path: apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-service.ts step (3) does `const dossier = readReleaseDossier(store, projectId, releaseDossierId(projectId, goalId, sha))` then `const markdown = dossier.dossier.markdown` — the STORED bytes. Step (5) passes `body: markdown` straight to `prPort.open`. The receipt's `dossierSha256(markdown)` is hashed from the SAME variable, so receipt hash and PR body hash are equal BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a second render agreeing with the first. The comment at step (5) states the hazard in as many words: "A second rendering is how a pull request and the durable record come to disagree about what was proven."
THE TEST DEFEATS ITS OWN VACUITY, which is the part worth reporting. release-decide-service.test.ts:280 "hands gh the STORED dossier bytes, identical to what the store reads back" opens with the exact objection I came to check (:290-291): "a fresh render of unchanged facts is byte-identical to the stored bytes, so 'body === the store read' passes whether the service reads the record or re-renders." It then DRIFTS the facts after storing — `goalTitle: "Retitled after the release record"` (:294) — pins that the drifted render differs from the stored bytes (:297), and asserts `request.body` still contains "Ship the release dossier" and `not.toContain("Retitled after the release record")` (:317-318), plus `toBe(readBack.dossier.markdown)` and a `Buffer.equals` (:310-313). A re-render would fail that arm. This is the single most important assertion in the feature and it is written correctly.
CORROBORATED LIVE, independently of the offline arm: on PR #33 the body's sha256 pulled over the GitHub API equals the receipt's dossierSha256 fbb2d0ad...5845 byte for byte, with CRLF-normalised and newline-shifted variants all differing (child task-817d893f's QA). Proof-carrying holds in fact, not only in the unit.

comments.author: worker-bcaa6d5e
comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL FINDING 1 of 2 (step 4(b), integration-level). THE RELEASE CARD TELLS THE OPERATOR THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE DAEMON WILL DO WHEN UNKNOWN > 0. Fail-closed, so no safety hole — a copy defect, filed here as a comment rather than a row per global rail 21 and step 4's own instruction.

WHAT THE CARD SAYS. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-release.tsx:115-120 renders, whenever summary.unknown !== 0:
  `UNKNOWN ${n} of ${total} · evidence for these criteria could not be re-measured. Approving releases them unverified.`
and the armed confirm label at :186 reads `Confirm: release ${covered} covered, ${unknown} UNKNOWN`. Both sentences promise the operator that pressing confirm RELEASES the unverified criteria.

WHAT THE DAEMON DOES. apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-service.ts step (2), before anything is pushed:
  const gaps = releaseDossierGaps(facts.input, sha, facts.ancestry);
  if (gaps.length > 0) { ... throw releaseRefusal("RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE", `unverified evidence for: ${criteria}`) }
So an APPROVE with any gap is REFUSED. It never releases them unverified — it releases nothing. A second, independent stop is one step later: apps/daemon/src/http/release-evidence-read.ts:9-10 records that a goal whose gaps are non-empty has NO STORED DOSSIER AT ALL, so step (3) would refuse RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE too.

WHY THE TWO SIDES CANNOT DISAGREE ABOUT THE CONDITION (which is what makes this a copy defect and not a race). The card's count is derived at goal-release.tsx:58 `covered = criteria.filter((row) => row.gaps.length === 0).length` from the rows `/release/read` serves, and release-evidence-read.ts:16-19 states the rows carry their own `gaps` and are never summed or booleanised there. The daemon's condition is `releaseDossierGaps(...).length > 0` over the same fold. So `cr.release.unknown` renders IF AND ONLY IF an approve would be refused. The sentence is never true when it is shown.

THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR WITHHOLDING THE OFFER. apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts:277-295 deliberately offers release.decide even with incomplete evidence, and says why: release's refusals ARE the operator's answer to "why can't I release?" — they name the criterion ids, the unbound remote, the missing dossier — so withholding would "replace a precise diagnostic with an absent card". That design is right and should stand. The card already renders the returned refusal (goal-release.tsx:165-167 `cr.release.refusal-code`, and goal-release.test.tsx carries five RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE assertions). Only the PRE-CONFIRM copy is wrong.

SUGGESTED WORDING, for whoever picks this up — a one-line change in the owning file, apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-release.tsx (owned by child task-817d893f):
  "... could not be re-measured. Approving will be refused RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE until they are."
and the armed label to something that does not promise a release, e.g. `Confirm: attempt release, ${unknown} UNKNOWN`.

COST OF LEAVING IT. An operator arms, confirms, and gets a refusal they were told would not happen; the natural reading is that the product is broken rather than that the evidence is short. It also trains the operator to treat UNKNOWN as a warning they may click through, which is exactly the habit the UNKNOWN/covered split exists to prevent.

NOT FIXED HERE: this row writes no production code (step 5's own instruction), and the change belongs to the row that owns the card.

comments.author: worker-bcaa6d5e
comments.content:
ADVERSARIAL FINDING 2 of 2 (step 4(c)+(d)). A REFUSED RELEASE RECEIPT DOES NOT SAY THAT A BRANCH WAS ALREADY PUSHED. The window is real, it is inherent (a push cannot be un-pushed), and the code handles it correctly — what is missing is that one durable record does not carry the fact the operator most needs from it.

THE WINDOW, on the delivered code (apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-service.ts). Step (4) calls `publisher.publishOnce()` — irreversible, the branch is now on the remote. Step (5) calls `prPort.open(...)`. Step (6): if `!opened.ok`, it writes `record("REFUSED", null, "RELEASE_PR_FAILED", markdown)` BEFORE throwing, with the comment "A refused release that recorded success is the worst thing this module could do". That ordering is right and is tested: release-decide-service.test.ts:333 sweeps three gh failure shapes (ENOENT spawn failure, `gh auth login required`, `pull request already exists`), asserts code RELEASE_PR_FAILED, asserts `refusal.layer` equals BOTH `RELEASE_DECIDE_CODE_LAYER_MAP.RELEASE_PR_FAILED` and the literal `"RUNNER_WORKSPACE"` (code AND layer, per global rail 1), asserts the stderr line is the detail, and closes with `expect(releasedReceiptCount(store)).toBe(0)` read back OUT of the store — its own comment calls that "POSITIVE ABSENCE", not a trusted return value.

THE GAP. `ReleaseReceiptV1` (release-receipt-contracts.ts:28-38) is exactly {decidedAt, dossierSha256, goalId, outcome, prUrl, projectId, receiptId, refusalCode, sha, version}. There is NO field recording that the push happened. So the durable release record of this window reads: outcome REFUSED, refusalCode RELEASE_PR_FAILED, prUrl null — indistinguishable, on its face, from a release that never touched the remote. The push IS durable, but in a DIFFERENT ledger (`moe-publish-receipt/1`, via readPublishLedger), so reconstructing "code is on the remote with no proof attached" requires joining two ledgers and knowing to. Nothing in the Release card does that join today.

(c) SHA DRIFT IS DETECTED — this is the good news and I checked it rather than assuming. `pushedBranchOf` (same file) accepts the LAST PUSHED receipt only when `receipt.sha === sha && receipt.remoteUrl === remoteUrl`, otherwise it yields null and the caller refuses. So if HEAD moved between the dossier build and the push, the publisher's receipt names the new sha, the equality fails, and no PR is opened from a tree the dossier does not describe. Tested at release-decide-service.test.ts:233 "refuses a branch whose latest pushed receipt names a different commit", with siblings at :380 (latest branch, not the first) and :395 (a PUSHED receipt with a null branch refuses rather than spawning `gh --head ""`). ANSWER TO STEP 4(c): the released dossier can never be attached to a different tree; the drift is caught before `gh` runs.
TWO RESIDUES from that, both minor and both in the same window as the finding above: (i) the sha-drift case is reported as RELEASE_PR_FAILED, whose detail comes from the publish report — semantically it is not a PR failure at all, and the closed three-code set has no code for "the sha moved under you". Widening the vocabulary is a contract change and is NOT proposed here; naming it in the detail string would be enough. (ii) a branch WAS pushed at the drifted sha, so this lands in the same push-with-no-PR state as (d).

WHAT DOES WORK ON RETRY: `releaseReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha, outcome, refusalCode)` keys on outcome AND refusalCode, so a REFUSED receipt does not collide with, or block, a later RELEASED one for the same sha. Re-approving after fixing `gh auth` succeeds and records properly. The sequential double-open is closed by the `alreadyReleased` check at step (4) plus test :411 "replays an already-RELEASED sha instead of opening a SECOND pull request".

STILL OPEN, RE-CONFIRMED ON THE DELIVERED CODE (not a new finding — child task-f961dc89's comment-6ee19c01): two SIMULTANEOUS approves can still double-open, because the `alreadyReleased` read happens BEFORE the push and there is no lock between the check and the write. Test :411 covers the SEQUENTIAL case only.

SUGGESTED, for whoever picks it up (owner: child task-f961dc89, apps/daemon/src/release/): add a `pushedBranch: string | null` (or `pushedSha`) to ReleaseReceiptV1 and populate it on the REFUSED path from `pushedBranchOf`, so one record answers "is my code on the remote with no PR attached?". Surface it on the card next to `cr.release.refusal-code`. NOT fixed here: this row writes no production code.
